items.name: Elks Most Valuable Student
items.summary: 500 four-year awards for seniors, judged on scholarship, leadership and financial need. U.S. citizens only; no Elks connection needed.

items.name: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship
items.summary: Last-dollar funding for high-achieving seniors with financial need, renewable through a bachelor's degree.

items.name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
items.summary: For Black/African American seniors showing academic excellence, leadership, community service and financial need.

items.name: Live Más Scholarship
items.summary: Passion-based: apply with a short video about what drives you instead of grades or test scores.

items.name: Voice of Democracy
items.summary: Audio-essay contest on a patriotic theme, entered through a local VFW Post. Local and state prizes too.

items.name: Coolidge Scholarship
items.summary: Full four-year merit scholarship for juniors with an interest in public policy, economics or the humanities.

items.name: Burger King Scholars
items.summary: Weighs GPA, work experience, activities, community service and need. Closes early once it hits its application cap.

items.name: Dell Scholars Program
items.summary: For Pell-eligible seniors in a college-readiness program, with a laptop, textbook credits and coaching through college.

items.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
items.summary: For students 18 or under who completed a significant project in STEM, literature, music or philosophy. 2027 application opens Nov 2.

items.name: HSF Scholar Program
items.summary: For students of Hispanic heritage with a 3.0+ GPA. Opens in January; needs a completed FAFSA.

items.name: Coca-Cola Scholars
items.summary: 150 seniors chosen for leadership and service impact. Opens each August; plan for next year if you're a junior.

items.name: The Gates Scholarship
items.summary: Last-dollar full scholarship for Pell-eligible minority seniors with strong academics and leadership.

items.name: QuestBridge National College Match
items.summary: Matches high-achieving, low-income seniors with full scholarships at partner colleges. Juniors can apply to the College Prep Scholars program in spring.

items.name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
items.summary: For seniors who have overcome significant adversity and show financial need and community involvement. The senior application runs December 1 to February 15.

items.name: National Merit Scholarship
items.summary: You enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT in October of junior year. Top scorers become Semifinalists the next fall.

items.name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
items.summary: The top research competition for seniors: submit an original science, math or engineering research project.

items.name: NCWIT Award for Aspirations in Computing
items.summary: Honors women, genderqueer and nonbinary students for computing achievements and interests. National and regional affiliate awards.

items.name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
items.summary: The longest-running recognition program for teen artists and writers. Regional deadlines are usually December–January.

items.name: YoungArts National Arts Competition
items.summary: For artists 15–18 in visual, literary, design and performing arts. Winners get cash awards and mentorship.

items.name: United States Senate Youth Program
items.summary: Two delegates per state, chosen from students in elected student-government or civic positions. Selection runs through the state.

items.name: Cal Grant (via FAFSA or CADAA)
items.amountText: Covers UC/CSU tuition or helps at private colleges
items.summary: California's state grant. You apply by filing the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application and a verified GPA by the state deadline.

items.name: Congressional Award
items.summary: Earn bronze to gold medals for goals in volunteer service, personal development, fitness and exploration. Your comp hours count.

items.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
items.org: Center for Excellence in Education at MIT
items.summary: Six-week summer research program at MIT for juniors. Free to students and highly selective.

items.name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
items.summary: Free six-week college-level seminar in critical Black studies or anti-oppressive studies for sophomores and juniors.

items.name: COSMOS
items.summary: Four-week residential STEM program at UC Irvine, Davis, San Diego or Santa Cruz for California students. Financial aid available.

items.name: MITES Summer
items.summary: Free six-week residential STEM program at MIT for rising seniors, especially those underrepresented in STEM.

items.name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
items.summary: Advanced summer math program covering abstract algebra, number theory and research-style problem solving.

items.name: Ross Mathematical Program
items.summary: Six-week number theory program built around deep problem sets. Known for teaching students to think like mathematicians.

items.name: PROMYS
items.summary: Six-week summer program in number theory with an application problem set.

items.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
items.summary: Five-week summer program where students choose their own advanced math classes. Entry is by a qualifying quiz.

items.name: UCSB Research Mentorship Program
items.summary: Six-week program pairing students with UCSB mentors on an interdisciplinary research project.

items.name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
items.summary: Free online programming contests held through the winter. Climb from Bronze to Platinum.

items.name: AMC 10/12
items.summary: The first round of the U.S. math olympiad pipeline, taken in November through your school or a host site.

items.name: Congressional App Challenge
items.summary: Build an app and submit it to your representative's district competition. Winners are shown in the Capitol. (comp. is an entry!)

items.name: Hack Club
items.summary: Nonprofit network of teen coders: start a club, join hackathons and "you ship, we ship" programs that fund your projects.

items.name: HOBY Leadership Seminar
items.summary: Weekend leadership seminar for sophomores, usually through a school nomination. Ask your counselor in the fall.

items.name: Boys State / Girls State
items.summary: A week building a mock state government, for juniors. Students are nominated through their school, usually in spring.

items.name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
items.summary: Rewards seniors who show ambition and self-drive through community impact. Hundreds of awards each year.

items.name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
items.summary: Four-year support, mentoring and career help for seniors of color with financial need and leadership potential.

items.name: APIA Scholars
items.summary: Scholarships for Asian American and Pacific Islander students, with priority for those with financial need.

items.name: UNCF Scholarships
items.summary: One application unlocks hundreds of scholarships, mostly for students attending UNCF member and other colleges.

items.name: Cameron Impact Scholarship
items.summary: Full-tuition merit scholarship for students with strong academics, leadership and community service. Apply the fall of senior year.

items.name: Gen and Kelly Tanabe Scholarship
items.summary: Short essay scholarship open to grades 9–12 with two rounds a year (winter and summer).

items.name: Doodle for Google
items.summary: Design a Google Doodle on the year's theme. The national winner's art appears on Google's homepage.

items.name: Profile in Courage Essay Contest
items.summary: Write about an elected official who showed political courage. Open to grades 9–12 nationwide.

items.name: Ayn Rand Essay Contests
items.summary: Essay contests on Anthem, The Fountainhead and Atlas Shrugged. Deadlines vary by book.

items.name: AFSA National High School Essay Contest
items.summary: Essay on diplomacy and U.S. foreign policy. The winner also gets a Semester at Sea voyage.

items.name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
items.summary: For seniors planning to study computer science, with a paid Amazon internship after freshman year.

items.name: Courage to Grow Scholarship
items.summary: Short essay scholarship awarded every month to juniors and seniors with a 2.5+ GPA.

items.name: Niche $10,000 No Essay Scholarship
items.summary: Random drawing with no essay. Open to high school and college students; a new drawing runs regularly.

items.name: SWE Scholarships
items.summary: Scholarships for women planning to study engineering or computer science in college.

items.name: Posse Scholarship
items.amountText: Full tuition at a partner college
items.summary: Nominated seniors go to a partner college in a group of 10 with full tuition. Nominations come from schools and community groups in Posse cities.

items.name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
items.summary: Give a speech on the U.S. Constitution. Local contests start in the fall and lead to nationals.

items.name: NHS Scholarship
items.summary: For senior NHS members, judged on scholarship, service, leadership and character.

items.name: Optimist International Essay Contest
items.summary: Essay contest for students under 19, entered through a local Optimist Club.

items.name: MIT THINK Scholars
items.summary: Propose a science or engineering project. Finalists get funding and mentorship from MIT students.

items.name: BU RISE Internship
items.summary: Six-week summer research internship in a Boston University lab for rising seniors.

items.name: NASA Internships
items.summary: Paid internships at NASA centers and virtually for students 16 and older. Spring, summer and fall sessions.

items.name: Army Educational Outreach Program
items.summary: Paid research apprenticeships and competitions in Army labs and universities.

items.name: JAX Summer Student Program
items.summary: Paid summer genetics research with a mentor at The Jackson Laboratory.

items.name: Summer Science Program
items.summary: Five-week research program in astrophysics, biochemistry or genomics. Need-based aid covers up to the full cost.

items.name: Yale Young Global Scholars
items.summary: Two-week academic program on Yale's campus for students from around the world. Generous financial aid.

items.name: Rise
items.summary: For ages 15–17. Winners get lifelong support, including scholarships and funding for service projects.

items.name: LEDA Scholars
items.org: Leadership Enterprise for a Diverse America
items.summary: Free summer program at Princeton plus college admissions coaching for high-achieving, low-income juniors.

items.name: NSLI for Youth
items.summary: Full scholarships to study critical languages (Arabic, Chinese, Korean and more) abroad for a summer or year.

items.name: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange
items.summary: Fully funded year living with a host family and attending school in Germany.

items.name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
items.summary: Free four-week engineering program (online course plus a summer project) for rising seniors.

items.name: Girls Who Code Summer Programs
items.summary: Free virtual summer coding programs and year-round clubs for girls and nonbinary students.

items.name: Kode With Klossy
items.summary: Free two-week summer coding camps for young women and gender-expansive youth ages 13–18.

items.name: Technovation Girls
items.summary: Teams of girls build a mobile app or AI project that solves a community problem.

items.name: picoCTF
items.summary: Free online cybersecurity capture-the-flag competition, plus year-round practice problems.

items.name: CyberPatriot
items.summary: Team cybersecurity competition where you secure virtual networks. Register as a school or club team.

items.name: Science Olympiad
items.summary: Team competition in 23 science and engineering events. Join through your school's team.

items.name: Regeneron ISEF
items.summary: The world's largest high school science fair. Qualify through a local or regional affiliated fair.

items.name: FIRST Robotics Competition
items.summary: Teams build and program a robot in six weeks each winter. Find or start a team near you.

items.name: USA Biology Olympiad
items.summary: Biology exam that selects the U.S. team for the International Biology Olympiad. Your school registers.

items.name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad
items.summary: Chemistry exam series that picks the U.S. team for the International Chemistry Olympiad.

items.name: F=ma and USAPhO
items.summary: Physics exams that select the U.S. Physics Team. Take F=ma through your school.

items.name: HMMT
items.summary: One of the biggest student-run math tournaments, held in November and February. Compete as a team.

items.name: Diamond Challenge
items.summary: Entrepreneurship competition for teens: pitch a business or social venture concept.

items.name: National History Day
items.summary: Research a historical topic and present it as a paper, exhibit, documentary, performance or website.

items.name: NYT Learning Network Contests
items.summary: Free contests all year: personal essays, editorials, podcasts, photos, and more.

items.name: John Locke Essay Competition
items.summary: International essay competition in philosophy, politics, economics, history and more.

items.name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
items.summary: Writing contest in poetry, fiction and nonfiction for grades 9–12.

items.name: VolunteerMatch on Idealist
items.summary: VolunteerMatch is now part of Idealist. Search local and virtual volunteer opportunities by cause and location.

items.name: DoSomething.org
items.summary: Youth-led campaigns for social change that you can join online or in your community. Some come with scholarships.

items.name: American Red Cross Youth Volunteering
items.summary: Help with blood drives, disaster preparedness and Red Cross clubs. Many roles are open to teens.

items.name: Habitat for Humanity Youth Programs
items.summary: Build homes with a local Habitat affiliate or start a campus chapter. Ages vary by affiliate.

items.name: Smithsonian Digital Volunteers
items.summary: Transcribe historical documents and specimen records online, on your own schedule.

items.name: Special Olympics
items.summary: Coach, partner or help at events with athletes with intellectual disabilities.

items.name: Volunteer at a Food Bank
items.summary: Find your local food bank to sort and pack food. Most welcome teen volunteers, some with a parent.

items.name: Key Club
items.summary: The largest student-led service organization. Join or start a club at your high school.
